properties.natural_language: Memory position popped from the stack must be a valid U256 value representable as a memory offset.
After memory expansion, all newly allocated bytes must be initialized to zero.
After a memory write operation (mstore/mstore8/mcopy), the written bytes at the target position must exactly match the source data.
After a memory read (mload), the value pushed to the stack must equal the 32 bytes starting at the specified memory position.
When mcopy source and destination ranges overlap, the operation must behave as if all source bytes are read before any destination bytes are written (memmove semantics).
Memory expansion gas cost must be charged before the memory operation is performed; insufficient gas must result in an out-of-gas exception.
Maximum memory size is implicitly bounded by the quadratic gas cost formula; no explicit size limit exists beyond gas constraints.
The memory_write and memory_read_bytes functions must correctly handle zero-length operations as no-ops.
After gas charge for mcopy, the total gas deducted must equal GAS_VERY_LOW + memory_expansion_cost + GAS_COPY * ceil32(length)/32.
After memory position validation, the position value must be within the U256 range.
The consolidation request must contain a valid source address (20 bytes), source pubkey (48 bytes), and target pubkey (48 bytes).
The fee payment accompanying a consolidation request must be greater than or equal to the computed consolidation fee from the exponential formula.
The consolidation request queue must not exceed 262,144 entries; requests exceeding this limit are discarded without fee refund.
After a successful system call, up to MAX_CONSOLIDATION_REQUESTS_PER_BLOCK (2) consolidation requests must be processed.
The predeploy contract at address 0x0000BBdDc7CE488642fb579F8B00f3a590007251 must exist and be immutable; absence makes the block invalid.
The validator balance received from the beacon chain must be at least MIN_ACTIVATION_BALANCE (32 ETH) for effective balance computation.
The computed effective balance must equal min(actual_balance, MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_ELECTRA) where MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_ELECTRA is 2048 ETH.
A validator exit request must include a valid validator index from the active validator set.
The per-epoch churn limit must be enforced: total exit weight processed in a single epoch must not exceed the churn budget (initially 256 ETH equivalent).
The consolidation fee must follow the exponential formula: fake_exponential(MIN_FEE, excess, UPDATE_FRACTION), ensuring fees increase exponentially with demand.
System call gas (30M) must be excluded from block gas limits and must not affect EIP-1559 base fee calculations.
An attacker cannot economically spam consolidation requests to fill the 262,144 queue due to exponential fee increases.
After checking compounding withdrawal prefix, validators with 0x02 prefix must have compounding enabled; others must use standard 32 ETH cap.
The transaction type byte must be one of the recognized types (0x00, 0x01, 0x02, or 0x03); unknown types must raise TransactionTypeError.
Blob transactions (type 0x03) must not attempt contract creation; such attempts must raise TransactionTypeContractCreationError.
Transaction max_fee_per_gas must be greater than or equal to the block base fee.
Transaction priority_fee_per_gas must not exceed max_fee_per_gas.
Blob transaction max_fee_per_blob_gas must be greater than or equal to the current blob base fee.
Blob versioned hashes must have correct version byte prefix (0x01), correct length (32 bytes), and valid KZG commitment correspondence.
Blob transactions must contain actual blob data; transactions claiming blobs without data must raise NoBlobDataError.
Contract creation init code must not exceed MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE.
Transaction data must be correctly deserialized from RLP before type-specific validation begins.
Block base fee must be correctly computed from parent block parameters before fee validation.
The EMPTY_ACCOUNT constant must have nonce=0, balance=0, and code=empty bytes; it must be used consistently across all code paths.
After account creation, the account must have initialized nonce, balance, and code fields.
After RLP encoding, the encoded bytes must deterministically represent [nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash].
The VersionedHash must have the correct version byte (0x01) as the first byte of the Hash32.
Two different valid Account values must never encode to the same byte representation in the state trie.
The Bytes, Uint, U256, Hash32 base types must correctly handle all edge cases including max/min values.
After a call-like opcode executes, the return data buffer must contain the complete return or failure data from the subcall.
The return data buffer must be cleared before executing any call-like opcode (CALL, DELEGATECALL, CREATE, etc.).
RETURNDATACOPY offset + length must not exceed RETURNDATASIZE and must not overflow; violation must trigger an out-of-gas exception.
Reading zero bytes from the end of the return data buffer (offset == RETURNDATASIZE, length == 0) must succeed as a valid empty read.
The return data buffer must be isolated per call frame and must not be accessible across different execution contexts.
A called contract must not be able to manipulate the caller's return data buffer except through normal return/revert mechanisms.
RETURNDATASIZE must consume exactly 2 gas and push the buffer size onto the stack.
RETURNDATACOPY gas cost must equal 3 + 3 * ceil(length / 32) plus memory expansion cost.
Attacker-controlled return data must be properly bounded by RETURNDATACOPY validation to prevent buffer overflow.
Block header must have sequential block number, increasing timestamp, valid gas limits, zero difficulty, zero nonce, and empty ommers hash.
Block difficulty field must equal zero (PoW removed in Paris/The Merge).
Block nonce field must be all zeros (no PoW nonce in PoS).
Block ommers hash must equal EMPTY_OMMER_HASH (keccak256 of empty RLP list: 0x1dcc4de8...).
After block body application, the computed state root, transaction root, receipt root, and logs bloom must match the header values.
Transaction sender must be recovered from signature, nonce must match, max_fee_per_gas >= max_priority_fee_per_gas, and balance must cover gas * max_fee + value.
After transaction execution, the gas refund must be capped at 20% of gas consumed (reduced from 50%).
After gas refund, the sender must receive back unused_gas * max_fee + (max_fee - effective_fee) * gas_used.
Base fee must increase when parent gas usage exceeds target and decrease when below target, with minimum adjustment of 1 wei for non-zero changes.
The beacon chain consensus layer must correctly validate blocks before passing execution payloads to the execution layer.
Base fee cannot be manipulated by attackers to destabilize the fee market; the 12.5% max change per block provides stability.
The 20% max gas refund must prevent refund-based DoS attacks through self-destructing contracts.
The Engine API communication between consensus and execution layers must be reliable and timely.
Transaction sender must be an externally owned account (EOA), not a contract.
The permission request object from the dApp must be a valid mapping of method names to caveat specifications.
User consent must be explicitly obtained via the permission prompt UI before any permission is granted.
After user rejection, the wallet must return JSON-RPC error code 4001 per EIP-1193.
An RPC method call must be checked for permission requirements before execution; restricted methods must have valid permission records.
Permission lookup must match both parentCapability (method name) and invoker (dApp origin).
All caveat constraints on a permission must be satisfied before allowing method execution.
wallet_getPermissions must return only permissions belonging to the requesting invoker, not permissions of other dApps.
URLs in permission requests must have an allowed scheme (http/https) and port; non-whitelisted schemes or ports must be blocked to prevent SSRF.
The wallet must correctly identify the invoker (dApp origin) without spoofing to prevent cross-origin permission theft.
Attackers must not be able to bypass the permission check by directly calling internal wallet methods.
The permission consent UI must not be susceptible to clickjacking or UI redressing attacks.
The wallet's permission storage must be protected from tampering by malicious extensions or local software.
Permissions must persist until explicitly revoked or wallet reset; implementers may add time-based expiration via caveats.
Hex input strings must contain only valid hexadecimal characters (0-9, a-f, A-F) after optional 0x prefix; invalid characters must cause a ValueError.
Hex integer input strings must be valid hexadecimal representations; the parsed value must fit within the target type bounds (U8, U64, U256, Uint).
Untrusted hex data at system boundaries must be validated and fixed-size padded before use; output must be exactly the required byte length.
After conversion, fixed-size byte outputs (Bytes8, Bytes32, Bytes256) must be exactly 8, 32, or 256 bytes respectively via zero-padding.
Python's int() base-16 parsing must handle arbitrarily large inputs without overflow; memory exhaustion from extremely large values is bounded by type wrappers.
Error handling for invalid hex characters must be properly propagated at trust boundaries to prevent denial of service.
Before precompile dispatch, the target address must be looked up in the PRE_COMPILED_CONTRACTS dictionary to determine if it is a precompile.
The PRE_COMPILED_CONTRACTS mapping must be immutable during execution; runtime modification would allow arbitrary code execution at precompile addresses.
Precompile addresses (0x01-0x0a) must not have regular contract code deployed to them; the precompile handler must always take precedence.
All precompile implementations must be correct and audited; bugs could break consensus or enable exploits.
The fork-specific precompile module must be correctly resolved during EVM initialization to ensure the right set of precompiles is active.
Gas for precompile execution must be charged by the precompile implementation itself; the mapping lookup is free.
After a memory write, the bytes at memory[start_position:start_position+length] must exactly equal the written data.
After a standard memory read, the returned bytes must equal memory[start_position:start_position+size].
After a buffered read with padding, out-of-bounds regions must be zero-padded on the right to the requested size.
After memory expansion, the new region must be initialized to all zeros and the gas cost must equal (words^2)/512 + 3*words.
Memory must be initialized to all zeros at the start of each call context to prevent data leakage between calls.
Sufficient gas must be charged before any memory operation is performed; operations without proper gas accounting must be rejected.
Maximum memory size is limited by quadratic gas cost formula; very large memory is practically infeasible within block gas limits.
The underlying bytearray implementation must be memory-safe and not vulnerable to buffer overflows.
Memory must return to idle state after both read and write operations complete.
Before memory expansion, the system must check if the access position exceeds current memory bounds.
After base gas calculation, the cost must be GAS_VERY_LOW for mstore/mstore8/mload/mcopy or GAS_BASE for msize.
For mcopy, the length parameter must be validated as a valid U256 value before bounds checking.
After memory read, the mload path must expand memory then read from the expanded region.
Gas for mcopy must include a copy cost component: GAS_COPY * ceil32(length)/32 in addition to base and expansion costs.
After consolidation fee computation, the fee amount must be determined by the exponential formula using current excess requests.
After successful fee validation, the request must be queued in the consolidation queue.
After exit weight computation, the weight must be checked against the epoch churn remaining budget.
After exit processing (full or partial), the validator must be moved to exiting status.
After balance validation, a balance below 32 ETH must result in the balance-below-minimum state.
After excess counter update, the new base fee must be computed via the exponential formula.
System call failure must make the entire block invalid.
After all fee validations pass, the transaction must transition to fees-valid state.
After successful type decode, the transaction type must be in the valid set.
After blob gas limit validation passes, the transaction proceeds to blob fee check.
After all blob-specific validations pass, the transaction reaches blob-validation-complete state.
After init code size validation passes, the transaction proceeds with valid init code.
After nonce update, the account's nonce must be incremented by exactly one.
After balance update, the account balance must reflect the value transfer amount.
After code deployment, the account's code field must contain the contract bytecode.
Account RLP encoding must include storage root and code hash computed from separate operations.
After KZG commitment computation and version prefix addition, the versioned hash must be a valid Hash32.
After RETURNDATASIZE execution, the buffer size must be read and pushed to the stack.
After RETURNDATACOPY, the specified bytes must be copied to EVM memory at destOffset.
After bounds violation, execution must halt with out-of-gas exception.
After a subcall executes and returns, the return data must be stored in the caller's buffer.
After RETURNDATACOPY gas charging fails, the operation must not proceed.
After header validation passes, the block proceeds to ommer validation.
After ommer validation, block body must be applied by executing all transactions.
After all PoS consensus checks pass, the consensus-valid state must be reached.
After transaction validation passes, gas * max_fee_per_gas must be deducted from sender upfront.
After priority fee payment and account cleanup, the transaction must reach complete state.
After root hash mismatch, the block must be marked invalid.
After gas target computation, block usage must be compared against target to determine fee adjustment direction.
After base fee computation and validation, the base-fee-valid state must be reached.
Transaction validation must check gas availability, recover sender, verify nonce, check fee relationships, verify balance, and confirm EOA status.
After user approves and permission is granted, the dApp must transition from connected to permission-granted state.
After permission check determines method is not restricted, it must be allowed without lookup.
After all caveats pass, method execution must be allowed.
The permission request data object and permission array must conform to the specified schema with method names and caveat specifications.
After URL scheme and port validation both pass, the URL must be marked as safe.
After prefix check, strings with '0x' prefix must have it removed; strings without must proceed directly to padding.
When an address is not a precompile, it must be treated as a regular contract call.
After fork-specific precompile availability check, the precompile is either dispatched or treated as empty account.
Precompile dispatch must route to the correct handler function based on address lookup.
After write range calculation, the start position and data length must be determined before write execution.
After memory access request, the system must determine the new required size before computing expansion cost.
Memory available for read must accept both standard reads and buffered reads with zero-padding.
